explanation: [[kw:Property tax]] is a tax on real estate (land and buildings) based on the assessed value of the property.
[[kw:Assessed value]] is a percentage of the property's market value, set by the local tax assessor.
$$\text{Assessed Value} = \text{Market Value} \times \text{Assessment Rate}$$
The tax rate is applied to the assessed value to determine the tax due.
[[imp:The assessment rate varies by locality; it's not the full market value.]]

blocks.title: 1. Assessed Value and Property Tax Basics

explanation: Property tax rates can be expressed in several equivalent ways:
- [[kw:Decimal]]: e.g., 0.025
- [[kw:Percent]]: 2.5% (decimal × 100)
- [[kw:Per $100]] of assessed value: $2.50 (percent × $1? Actually: per $100 = percent rate × $100? Wait: 2.5% means $2.50 per $100. So per $100 = percent rate (as number) = 2.5.)
- [[kw:Mills]]: 25 mills (1 mill = $1 per $1,000; so mills = per $1,000 rate)
[[imp:Mills are often used by local governments; 1 mill = $0.001 or $1 per $1,000.]]

visuals.title: Calculating Property Tax ($120,000 assessed, 25 mills)
visuals.caption: All methods yield the same tax amount.

explanation: To compute the property tax, multiply the assessed value by the tax rate (in decimal form).
$$\text{Property Tax} = \text{Assessed Value} \times \text{Tax Rate (decimal)}$$
If the rate is given per $100: $$\text{Tax} = \frac{\text{Assessed Value}}{100} \times \text{Rate per } \$100$$
If given in mills: $$\text{Tax} = \text{Assessed Value} \times \frac{\text{Mills}}{1{,}000}$$
[[imp:Always convert the rate to decimal form before multiplying, unless using the per $100 or per $1,000 shortcut.]]

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Property Tax} = \text{Assessed Value} \times \text{Tax Rate (decimal)}$$ $$\text{or}$$ $$\text{Tax} = \frac{\text{Assessed Value}}{100} \times \text{Rate per } \$100$$ $$\text{or}$$ $$\text{Tax} = \frac{\text{Assessed Value}}{1{,}000} \times \text{Mills}$$

formulaCard.title: Conversion Formulas

explanation: Conversions are straightforward:
- Decimal to percent: multiply by 100; add % symbol.
- Percent to decimal: divide by 100.
- Percent to per $100: same number (e.g., 2.5% = $2.50 per $100).
- Per $100 to per $1,000: multiply by 10.
- Per $1,000 to mills: same number.
- Mills to decimal: divide by 1,000.
[[imp:Memorize: mills = dollars per $1,000.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: A homeowner's property has a market value of $400,000, an assessment rate of 50%, and a tax rate of 30 mills. Use the blueprint to calculate the annual property tax.

explanation: Apply the blueprint to property tax problems:
1. Understand: identify market value, assessment rate, and tax rate (in any form).
2. Solve: compute assessed value, convert tax rate to decimal if needed, then compute tax. Use the method that matches the given rate (decimal, per $100, mills).
3. Conclude: state the property tax amount; verify that the calculation used the correct base (assessed, not market).
This structured approach prevents errors like applying tax to market value or misinterpreting mills.
